kat: pyfe4ai bcfe half-gates garbling, known answers
construction: half gates (Zahur, Rosulek, Evans, EUROCRYPT 2015, Fig. 2) on CIRC v1 circuits, free XOR, point-and-permute; reference pyfe4ai.primitives.garbling

derivation.salt: SHAKE-256(dst.kat_salt || name)[0:56] (opaque to the garbling; the scheme's salt is pp_digest || ct_nonce || u64(slot_id))
derivation.x: the first n bits of SHAKE-256(dst.kat_x || name), LSB of each byte first
derivation.w: the first m bits of SHAKE-256(dst.kat_w || name) (m: key bits of C), then g = 0
derivation.random circuits: gen_kat.random_circuit(name): SHAKE-256(dst.kat_circuit || name) read as u32 LE words, rejection sampled; the encoding is stored

conventions.circuit: every case garbles guard(C) (SS10 g bit = key wire m of C); circuit.encoding / circuit.digest are those of guard(C), unguarded_* those of C (what pp binds); library circuits are pyfe4ai.circuits.<function>(**params).circuit
conventions.bits: x, w and outputs are strings of 0/1, character i = wire / output i; w has the m + 1 key bits of guard(C), g last
conventions.packed: x_packed and decode: bits packed LSB first (spec 3.7)
conventions.labels: 16-byte strings; key_active[j] = key0[j] xor w_j * delta; in mode labels data_active is returned by the garbling, in mode hardwired it is empty
conventions.seed expansion: SHAKE-256(dst.garbling_prg || salt(56) || seed(32)) read as delta (then delta[0] |= 1), key0 per key wire, the data wires' zero labels (mode labels)
conventions.sha256: SHA-256 of the raw bytes of key0, data_active, tables
conventions.output: evaluation of the garbling with the labels of w, decoded; plain_output: guard(C)(w, x) in the clear; output_by_w[v]: the output for the key bits of the integer v (LSB = wire 0), same garbling
